empty_space.where: Bottom of Column 2 and Column 3, leaving about 13% of the canvas unused, which creates an unbalanced look.
empty_space.effect: The poster looks incomplete and poorly balanced.

small_visual_text.where: Figure 3 (SHAP beeswarm plot) y-axis labels and Figure 1 y-axis labels.
small_visual_text.effect: The specific biomarker names and feature descriptors are too small to read from a normal viewing distance of 1–2 meters.

unclear_order.where: Column 1, where the flow goes Abstract -> Figure 2 -> Introduction -> Table 1.
unclear_order.effect: The reader is forced to look at results (Figure 2) before the Introduction, which disrupts the logical flow of the research narrative.

missing_sections.where: The headings present are Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, and Conclusion. The Discussion section is missing.
missing_sections.effect: There is no dedicated space to discuss the implications, limitations, or future work of the study.

thin_sections.where: All sections (Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Conclusion) consist of only one or two short sentences.
thin_sections.effect: With only 273 words on the entire poster, the research is not sufficiently explained; a reader cannot understand the cohort details, feature engineering, or model training without reading the paper.

layout.reason: The layout has a highly unconventional and confusing reading order in the first column (Abstract -> Figure 2 -> Introduction -> Table 1), is missing a Discussion section, and features extremely thin sections that fail to explain the research depth.

readability.reason: While the main body text is large and easy to read, the text labels in Figure 3 (SHAP plot) and Figure 1 are far too small to be legible at a standard viewing distance.

fidelity.reason: The poster accurately highlights the primary findings, including the LightGBM AUROC of 0.797, the prediction horizon analysis, and the SHAP feature importances.

holistic.reason: The poster needs substantial rework because its sections are far too thin to explain the research (containing only 273 words in total), and the reading order in the first column is highly illogical.
